headline: PSX slips as Habib Metro's earnings miss and a stalled Ascon takeover overshadow a calm global tape and a still-favoured bank carry trade.
summary: PSX closed slightly lower today, weighed down by Habib Metro's 19% first-half profit drop and SECP suspending Ascon Consulting's stake-acquisition deal. Globally the backdrop stayed calm — low volatility, firm US equities — though oil is still up on the month and gold's safe-haven bid keep the desk's risk gauge at a moderate 46/100. The macro picture is neutral: State Bank held rates at 11.5%, inflation cooled to 9.2%, and T-bill yields near 11.7% keep the bank carry trade attractive. A widely reported fiscal-deficit figure is conflicting across sources, so the desk isn't treating it as confirmed. Net: cautious, quality-first positioning.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: T-bill yields near 11.7% sit well above the held 11.5% policy rate, and most large lenders (ABL, BAHL, BOP, FABL, MCB, NBP, UBL, HMB) screen cheap with covered dividends — though HMB's -19% first-half profit miss today is a live reminder that results season can bite even a favoured sector.

sectors.name: OMCs & refining
sectors.why: Brent is still up almost 5% over the month even after today's pullback, and PSO, PRL, NRL and ATRL only rate 'mixed' on fundamentals — cheap-looking multiples sit on thin margins exposed to the daily fuel-price mechanism.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Firm crude helps OGDC, PPL, MARI and POL's earnings, but all four rate only 'mixed' on valuation, not cheap, and POL's technicals already look overbought.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: FCCL just posted its highest-ever annual profit, but it still only rates 'mixed' on fundamentals (thin dividend, fair price) — the sector's earnings momentum is real, the valuation cushion is not.

watchlist.angle: The desk's strongest current setup: a volume-leads-price signal (obv_divergence_up) just fired, and on BML's own 89-trade history that pattern has won 97% of the time for +5.1% net per trade, still 83% out-of-sample. Fundamentals back it up — cheap at roughly 6.7x earnings with a strong 32% net margin. Results are estimated for around Aug 28, though that date is an unconfirmed scraped estimate.
watchlist.risk: It pays no dividend, so the whole return depends on price follow-through, and it's a smaller name outside the KSE-100 — thinner liquidity than the big-name banks.

watchlist.angle: A momentum-acceleration signal (roc_accel) has triggered, though the backtest is thin — 54 trades, 59% hit rate, a modest edge, and the desk rates its own confidence in this one low. Fundamentals lean supportive: cheap around 5.5x earnings with an even cheaper forward multiple, though the dividend is small. Results are pencilled in for late September on an unconfirmed date.
watchlist.risk: Low sample size and low confidence on the backtest; as an auto-sector name it's exposed to import-cost and rupee swings that could snap the momentum before the thesis plays out.

catalysts.event: MSCI Frontier Small Cap reconstitution effective (AIRLINK added, Biafo removed)
NICL and PPL results (estimated dates, unconfirmed)

risks: Oil creeps back up: Brent is still +4.84% on the month after fresh Gulf/Red Sea attack headlines, and a renewed spike would widen the import bill and pressure the rupee, hurting OMC margins and the wider market.

The fiscal-deficit story is unreconciled — one report cites a 22-year-low 2.6% of GDP, another a wider ~3.6% figure — and a confirmed worse number later could dent confidence in the reserves/IMF narrative underpinning the neutral regime.
Bank results season disappointments could spread: HMB's -19% year-on-year first-half miss today tests the sector's 'favoured' carry-trade thesis just as other large lenders are still due to report.
